dedupe_keys.name: portugal waste bin fill monitoring with ultrasonic sensors versus truck driver observations

description: This case study compares two ways of knowing how full waste bins are before collection, using data from a Portuguese waste management company. The authors, from Instituto Superior Técnico of the University of Lisbon and the University of Coimbra, analysed bin fill level readings from ultrasonic sensors installed in bins and the visual observations recorded by collection truck drivers, then applied a Gaussian process prediction model to explore the trade-off between the number of collections and the number of overflows under each approach. The article was published in 2023 in Waste Management and Research and is free to read online in PubMed Central under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Coverage is the collection area of one Portuguese operator. Caveats: the data belong to the company and are not published, and the results depend on how consistently drivers record observations. The study found that driver observations are valuable, that either approach combined with prediction could cut collections and overflows compared with current practice, and that observations plus a predictive model are a viable low-cost step while operators move towards fully sensorised bins. Simulation uses: evidence on monitoring options and overflow and collection trade-offs for waste collection optimisation models. Related records: the COMPOSITION bin fill level sensor readings (data-composition-bin-fill-level-sensors) are an open sensor dataset of the same kind.
